description: This provisional sweep contains 19 original captured search actions with 507 ordered result headers: 16 English-language and 3 Arabic-language queries spanning broad February coverage, Tripoli, labor and student leads, the Military Court, Beirut blast victims, Lokman Slim, Bkerki, economic protest and month boundaries. It is not an exhaustive archive review or LexisNexis-equivalent; French and other local-language coverage, regional outlets, official records and organizer materials remain incomplete. Search headers are discovery only.
required_followup: Continue language- and region-specific open-web research and consult eligible archives and primary records when available; preserve every original result and avoid claims of absence or exhaustiveness.

description: The January Lebanon dossier records a Jan. 25–28 Tripoli lockdown/economic sequence with conflicting consecutive-day descriptions and an unknown physical end, plus a possible Jan. 31 Al-Nour resumption after a reported lull. This February dossier has search-only Beirut/Tripoli anti-lockdown and Tripoli restaurant-worker leads (S001–S003), but no opened evidence establishes a February physical action continuous with January or its onset/end. No continuation is asserted and no January candidate is copied or merged. February physical gatherings, if verified, need their own evidence-based onset and boundaries.
required_followup: Check contemporaneous reports for the exact February date, location and physical action, then distinguish a new dated gathering from an uninterrupted continuation; do not infer continuity from a shared city, demand or lockdown context.

description: Search-only headers identify demonstrations in Beirut and Tripoli against lockdown and hardship (S001) and a Tripoli restaurant/cafe worker sit-in lead (S002–S003). The body was not read; the February physical onset, actual turnout, exact demand, organizers, event boundaries and State response are unverified. The title/URL alone does not establish that any gathering met the 50-person threshold or that the worker action was the same event as a broader demonstration.
required_followup: Use fresh exact-URL access reviews to read relevant contemporaneous reports; establish each gathering's date, participant threshold, demand and boundary separately before adding an event.

description: S008 verifies one Beirut Military Court sit-in on Feb. 15 demanding release of people arrested after Tripoli riots, but says only “a number of protesters”; attendance remains below the evidence needed to establish 50. Search-only reports S005–S007 and S009–S012 point to other court-related gathering leads, some with larger headline estimates. S005 and S012 were duplicate capture cards for the same exact MTV URL and represent one page, not independent corroboration. No opened evidence verifies those leads’ counts, exact physical boundaries or relationship to the Feb. 15 sit-in. No multi-day campaign or turnout is transferred between reports.
required_followup: Seek event-specific reports with reliable attendance and date evidence; keep separate dated physical gatherings separate unless continuity is supported.

description: Search-only reports S013–S019 point to family members of Beirut port-blast victims gathering near the Justice Palace after investigative judge Fadi Sawan was removed. Their exact February physical onset, attendance, demand directed to the Lebanese State, duration and State response have not been verified from opened sources.
required_followup: Read event-day accounts or statements that establish the actual gathering, date, demand and participant threshold; retain any search-only estimate as unverified.

description: Search-only reports S020–S024 identify possible public gatherings after Lokman Slim's killing and memorial activity in Beirut. No opened account establishes a February physical gathering's onset, attendance, demand to the Lebanese State, or whether memorial attendance constituted an eligible protest action.
required_followup: Locate contemporaneous event reports and distinguish memorial observance from a public gathering making a demand to the State; do not infer eligibility from topic or attendance at a funeral.

description: The opened Feb. 27 Bkerki report supports a physical rally and describes its crowd qualitatively: its headline says 'Thousands' while the body says 'a large number' with no count or method. It describes support for Patriarch Bechara al-Rahi's policy calls to Lebanese officials, but the quoted spokesperson says the event was not political. Whether the rally itself made an eligible demand to the State remains unresolved. The physical end and State response are unreported.
required_followup: Seek independent contemporaneous attendance and event-purpose evidence and any direct account of the gathering's end or State response; retain pending_state_target unless its own demand is established.

description: S029 is a search-only LAU student daily sit-in lead with no verified February date, participant threshold, exact demand or State response. The labor, currency and issue-specific queries also do not establish additional February mass gatherings from opened evidence. This means no qualifying event was verified in those searches, not that no action occurred.
required_followup: Check event-day school, union and local coverage for actual in-person gatherings, dates, thresholds and government-directed demands; keep announcements and search-only claims out of confirmed coding.

description: Eight physical body requests were attempted across five URLs; two article bodies were read: The961 S027 and LBCI S008. Two exact-URL attempts each for Lebanon24 S002, Lebanese Forces S030 and IMLebanon S003 failed technically (a web-tool Cache miss followed by ordinary HTTPS DNS lookup failure for each), with no HTTP status or body; these are not denials. The other 27 of 29 unique-URL source cards remain search_only. ArabicPost S001 was not requested after manual review found a possible relationship to an ArabicPost-labeled URL with a prior 403 on arabicpost.live, while no explicit alias or shared publisher scope was documented for stage.arabicpost.net; no alias was inferred. Four stale receipts (two The961 and two Lebanese Forces after peer source-ledger hashes changed), one initial deferred gate, and a later MTV receipt that deferred during an input change resulted in no body requests. An earlier MTV manual_review receipt was unused and did not authorize a request. ArabicPost was separately left unrequested after its ambiguous scope review. Search-only titles/snippets do not support event facts.
required_followup: Keep ambiguous ArabicPost scope unresolved and honor any observed restriction. For every new body request, save a fresh exact-URL receipt, complete manual publisher/origin review, then recheck the full saved input set immediately before requesting.

description: Neither current candidate has an evidenced physical end date. E001's article calls the rally peaceful but does not report a State response; E002's short report does not characterize protester conduct or State response. Unknown values remain unknown rather than inferred from silence or from events on other dates.
required_followup: Seek event-specific sources for physical end and government response; retain null end dates and unknown response dimensions until sourced.
